The Patient Prescription Insights program provides feedback about XARTEMIS XR to doctors, through the voice of their own patients.

 

Key points:

1.       A great way to get quick feedback on how your patients feel about this new treatment option

2.       Patients value both the copay savings as well as the opportunity to give you feedback

3.       [Referring to sample report] This is an example of the kind of input you ll get from your own patients

4.       No extra work is required   simply give your patients the Kit with the prescription and we take care of the rest

 

Steps:

1.       Introduce the Program by closing your detail with an introduction of the XARTEMIS XR Patient Prescription Insights Program and drop off <5?> - remove the number as it will vary according to potential patient kits.

2.       Gain Commitment from the doctor and office staff to participate in the program and invite eligible patients to enroll in the Program.

3.       Return <One Week> - OK Later and encourage the doctor to give a patient kit to patients who receive a script for XARTEMIS XR.

4.       Return again and continue to encourage the doctor to give the patient kits to patients who receive a script for XARTEMIS XR.

 

How it works:

         At the end of your sales call, you will introduce the program to your Healthcare Professional and drop off the kits

         Doctors will be automatically enrolled in the program via a data feed from your <SFA> system after you drop off the kits.

         Doctors will receive a welcome letter with a sample report to remind them about the program.

         The patient is provided the XARTEMIS XR Starter Kit along with their script. It contains specific enrollment directions

         Patients enroll in the survey and complete the survey online or on the phone. Surveys assess treatment experience and satisfaction

         Doctors receive a report of their patient s responses to the surveys

Benefits for you:

         Positively impacts your sales- reword  by establishing your credibility and interest in promoting patient education and communication between patient and Healthcare Professional

         Provides an effective tool to impact prescribing behavior among Healthcare Professionals in your territory by creating brand impressions even when you aren t detailing them

         Creates an opportunity to reach Healthcare Professionals and encourage them to prescribe XARTEMIS XR and see what their patients  experiences are.

Your role:

         Close your detail with the program flashcard, and leave it with the office.

         Encourage Healthcare Professionals to give their patients a XARTEMIS XR Starter Kit that s all they have to do

         Follow up with offices to keep the program top of mind!

Benefits for Healthcare Professionals:

         Increases confidence in writing XARTEMIS XR by allowing Healthcare Professionals to receive feedback from patients who have had a positive experience on it

         Personalized feedback reports help Healthcare Professionals keep track of patients  unique treatment experiences

         Encourages helpful dialogue during follow-up appointments

Tips for making the program a success:

 
          Highlight the sample report on the flashcard so that Healthcare Professionals see the value of the information they will receive

          Remind Healthcare Professionals that the program is easy:  The Healthcare Professional hands a starter kit (with enclosed program invitation) to a patient

          The patient enrolls online or by phone and takes a brief survey about their experience with XARTEMIS XR

o   Assure Healthcare Professionals that the program is strictly confidential patients  personal information and reports will not be shared with anyone but them

Increase your credibility and value by offering a service Healthcare Professionals truly value and appreciate.

text:
From:Stewart, Cathy
To:Kaiman, Vince J; Gunning, Michael L; Neely, Mike; Polizzi, Marco F; Burd, Jeff W MKG; Werder, Sue
A

CC:Ratliff, Bill; Harper, Karen; Pheney, Michael; Levy, JoAnne; Rausch, Jim H; Stewart, Cathy
Sent:5/14/2008 6:11:30 PM
Subject:DEA Suspicious Order Quantities
I wanted to advise all of you that we re working with Security and the DEA Compliance  Group (Bill Ratliff
and Karen Harper) to develop procedures to insure we maintain compliance with the DEA  requirement
that we report any suspicious order quantities and/or patterns to them. In light of  the recent
developments with McKesson, a good deal of focus is being placed on this project.
Briefly, if an order is deemed  peculiar  by a customer service rep based on a set of  guidelines currently
being developed, it will be placed on hold and the DEA compliance group (Bill Ratliff  and Karen Harper)
will be advised. DEA Compliance will then conduct a more in-depth investigation and determine if the
situation warrants notification to the DEA. If the order is deemed appropriate, customer service will be
notified and the order will be released from hold status for shipment. If the outcome of the investigation
supports that the order is in fact  suspicious  it will not be shipped and the local  DEA office will be notified.
 I would expect that we also develop a means of communication to the business group any time an order
is placed on hold for reasons of peculiarity by the Customer Service Group. Updates  regarding the status
of specific orders should be forwarded as well as the  peculiar order  proceeds through the review process.
Preliminary processes are in development and I m in the process of determining/evaluating how best to
identify deviations from the norm based on the type of businesses we service as well as the products being
purchased. Criteria that is well suited for an AT Clinic may be too stringent for a Distributor. Each class of
customer (clinics, distributors, wholesalers, etc.) will be handled based on the merits of the business
segment they support. Any anomalies that support what we term as a  peculiar  order will be forwarded
to the DEA compliance group for further investigation prior to it being turned over to the DEA.
As these respective formulas are developed, I will share them with you along with a sampling of data used
to support the validity/effectiveness of the assumptions used in developing same. At first pass, the
formula might look like this:
- Customers will be separated into their respective class of business (distributors, wholesalers, clinic, hospitals,
retail, etc)
- Add purchase quantities, by product (all Oxy products and again by individual skus) for the last 12 months
for all customers within the same class of business for any controlled substances
o  Customer s with multiple  ship to  locations should have their total aggregated at the  sold to  level;
but also reviewed at the  ship to  level
- Add customer months for every record used in the above total (months within the last 12 that customer
purchases of the item were not zero)
- Divide total quantity purchases by the total customer months
- Then multiply by the factor below to give the maximum mount that the customer can order per month
before showing up on the suspicious order report.
o  Factor = 2 for C-II Controlled Substances
o  Factor = 4 for C-III, IV and V
Once the myriad aspects of this project are refined, selective excess order quantity business rules may


   require adjustment.
In addition to order quantities by product, we hope to also develop criteria for orders that deviate from
normal ordering patterns and/or from usual order frequency (not yet sure how to capture this; hope to
identify an algorithm that will support parsing through the data to identify patterns, frequency, etc.) A
report will be generated daily (at a minimum) but hope to eventually have the systems  in place so
customer service receives a  real time  flag when an order violates one of our parameters and will flag the
order as peculiar.
The group is working on other indicators that might be used in evaluating whether or not a customer
should be reported as  peculiar . The Sales force will play a key role in this process by verifying the
customer s physical site and operations ring true with the type of business they purport to run. The DEA
Compliance group is in the process of discussing this aspect with management on the Sales side of the
business.
If you have any questions, please let me know. This process is in preliminary stages  so we may not have
answers to all the questions that may come up, but those questions might also be food  for thought in
furthering the breadth of this project.
Regards,

Thanks Lisa.

These orders hit the "threshold limit". I will probably butcher this, but here goes:

The report is looking at the previous 18 months of orders (product specific) for an average. It is them
multiplied by 3. this is called the "target average qty", which is an acceptable amou nt. Keep in mind they
are measured by molecule of the product family and not on skus.
The "target average qty" for hydromorphone is 106, actual order qty is 149 (again this is measured by
molecule)
The "target average qty" for morphine is 960, actual order qty is 1392 (molecules again)

This is not a very technical way of describing the process, but it is how I understand it.

This is just one of several formulas used on the report.

DEA Compliance Procedure   No:
Subject:  Revision  No.:
 1
Controlled Substance Suspicious Order Monitoring  Effective Date:

 Supersedes Date:
NEW
 Page No.:
1  of 3

Originator: Security:
Karen Harper
Corporate Logistics: Documentation Coordinator:


PURPOSE:
Establish a procedure to identify and report controlled substance suspicious orders  to the Drug
Enforcement Administration
SCOPE:
Applies to establishing a new controlled substance customer account and subsequent shipment of
all controlled substance orders to new or established customers.
REFERENCES:
Title 21 CFR 1301.74(b)
The registrant shall design and operate a system to disclose to the registrant suspicious orders of
controlled substances. The registrant shall inform the Field Division Office of the Administration
in his area of suspicious orders when discovered by the registrant. Suspicious  orders include
orders of unusual size, orders deviating substantially from a normal pattern, and orders of
unusual frequency..
DEFINITIONS:
Peculiar Order   A controlled substance order that meets and internal, established criteria
that will be placed on  hold  pending further review by DEA Compliance.
Suspicious Order  A controlled substance Peculiar Order that has been reviewed by DEA
Compliance and Security that will not be shipped and will be reported to
the Drug Enforcement Administration.


   QSP 00.00  Rev 1  TITLE  2  of 3


RESPONSIBILITIES:
Credit Department or Customer Data Integrity Group
Perform Dun & Bradstreet information check on new controlled substance customers to
determine credit worthiness.
Refer  the new customer account to Security Director or DEA Compliance if the new account has
no historical or financial information available or if the data shows liens, lawsuits, or other
information which might raise suspicions as to the legitimacy  of the new account company.
Conduct periodic checks on our  existing customers if they ve been put on credit hold two times
in the previous 12 months.
Field Sales
Completes Site Survey Checklist for New Controlled Substance Customers (Attachment A)
Customer Service Representative
Completes Controlled Substance Order Checklist (Attachment B) and refers orders that meet the
Peculiar Order criteria to DEA Compliance and Security Director for review
Customer Service Manager
Obtains a daily report from the order entry system that highlights orders deviating in qua ntity
from an established order pattern calculation to determine if order quantity fits Peculiar Order
criteria and refers to DEA Compliance and Security Director for review
Security Director

DEA Compliance Procedure   No:
Subject:  Revision  No.:
 1
Controlled Substance Suspicious Order Monitoring  Effective Date:

 Supersedes Date:
NEW
 Page No.:
1  of 3

Originator: Security:
Karen Harper
Corporate Logistics: Documentation Coordinator:


PURPOSE:
Establish a procedure to identify and report controlled substance suspicious orders  to the Drug
Enforcement Administration
SCOPE:
Applies to establishing a new controlled substance customer account and subsequent shipment of
all controlled substance orders to new or established customers.
REFERENCES:
Title 21 CFR 1301.74(b)
The registrant shall design and operate a system to disclose to the registrant suspicious orders of
controlled substances. The registrant shall inform the Field Division Office of the Administration
in his area of suspicious orders when discovered by the registrant. Suspicious  orders include
orders of unusual size, orders deviating substantially from a normal pattern, and orders of
unusual frequency..
DEFINITIONS:
Peculiar Order   A controlled substance order that meets and internal, established criteria
that will be placed on  hold  pending further review by DEA Compliance.
Suspicious Order  A controlled substance Peculiar Order that has been reviewed by DEA
Compliance and Security that will not be shipped and will be reported to
the Drug Enforcement Administration.


   QSP 00.00  Rev 1  TITLE  2  of 3


RESPONSIBILITIES:
Credit Department or Customer Data Integrity Group
Perform Dun & Bradstreet information check on new controlled substance customers to
determine credit worthiness.
Refer  the new customer account to Security Director or DEA Compliance if the new account has
no historical or financial information available or if the data shows liens, lawsuits, or other
information which might raise suspicions as to the legitimacy  of the new account company.
Conduct periodic checks on our  existing customers if they ve been put on credit hold two times
in the previous 12 months.
Field Sales
Completes Site Survey Checklist for New Controlled Substance Customers (Attachment A)
Customer Service Representative
Completes Controlled Substance Order Checklist (Attachment B) and refers orders that meet the
Peculiar Order criteria to DEA Compliance and Security Director for review
Customer Service Manager
Obtains a daily report from the order entry system that highlights orders deviating in qua ntity
from an established order pattern calculation to determine if order quantity fits Peculiar Order
criteria and refers to DEA Compliance and Security Director for review
Security Director
Provides Site Survey Checklist for New Controlled Substance Customers to be completed by
Field Sales
Reviews results of Site Survey Checklist for New Controlled Substance Customers and provides
authorization to proceed with new customer account set-up
In conjunction with DEA Compliance, reviews controlled substance or ders that have been
identified as Peculiar Orders by Customer Service and makes the ship or do not ship decision
Reports orders deemed Suspicious to the Drug Enforcement Administration
DEA Compliance
Provides updated  Drugs of Concern  listing to Customer  Service quarterly
Provides Controlled Substance Order Checklist to Customer Service


  QSP 00.00  Rev 1  TITLE  3  of 3

In conjunction with Security Director, reviews controlled substance orders that have been
identified as Peculiar Orders by Customer Service and makes the ship or do not ship decision
Reports orders deemed Suspicious to the Drug Enforcement Administration.
Maintains a file at the St. Louis Plant Site for record retention of Suspicious Order Monitoring
documents and reports.

Subject: Crossroads Recovery DEA Reg# RC0270974



 

Heather,


 


Attached is supporting documentation of suspicious activity we have discovered surrounding the sale of Crossroads Recovery, Inc. in Dallas, TX with the following details for your consideration:


 


·         Controlled Substance Compliance was notified by our credit department that customer Crossroads Recovery, Dallas TX (DEA Reg# RC0270974) had an outstanding bill that was in dispute between the old owners of the NTP clinic and the new owners of clinic from February 2010. 

·         The clinic was sold by Diane Day and purchased by Joseph Baiamonte and Frances McGrady.  The sales contract is dated February 15, 2010.  Attached is a letter from the new owners with specific pages from the sales contract, it is not inclusive.  Cover letter provided by the purchasers state that they did not close on the sales contract until February 19, 2010 and that they were not responsible for any fees until March 1, 2010. 

·        A letter was sent to Mallinckrodt on march 8, 2010 from Diane Day (attached) updating Joseph Baiamonte and Francis McGrady as being authorized to order and receive methadone, however it does not state that the clinic was sold or transferred ownership.  Thus, we did not change any of our accounts as the current DEA Registration for Crossroads Recovery was in effect until August 31, 2010 and we simply thought they were updating their authorized signors list.

·         Attached are also copies of 2 different 222 forms, one from February and one from March.  The March invoice has been paid, the February invoice has not and was the cause for the sale to be brought to our attention.  Based on the signature of the sales contract it appears that Diane Day did sign the 222 form from February 17, 2010, however it appears that someone else could have potentially signed Diane Day's name on the March 222 form with their initials after her name.  Mallinckrodt continued to ship at this time as we had not been made aware of the change of ownership and 222 used to order was for the same DEA Reg# RC0270974 currently on file.

·         A review of shipping records from March 1, 2010 to date, shows 4 orders have been shipped, all using the DEA Reg# RC0270974 and sequential DEA Form 222 numbers.  The March order was signed with the name Diane Day and the subsequent 3 orders (May, June, August) were signed by Lillian Williams McGrady.

As part of our ongoing Suspicious Order Monitoring program, Mallinckrodt will be incorporating the requirement for any clinic to provide proof of ownership and/or sale immediately upon notification to us of the sale of a NTP clinic.


 


Please do not hesitate to contact me if I can provide further information or any assistance.

Cc:  Ratliff, Bill <Bill.Ratliff@Covidien.com>; Harper, Karen <Karen.Harper@Covidien.com>; Pheney, Michael <Michael.Pheney@Covidien.com>; Levy, JoAnne <JoAnne.Levy@Covidien.com>; Rausch, Jim H <Jim.Rausch@Covidien.com>; Stewart, Cathy <Cathy.Stewart@Covidien.com>
Subject:  DEA Suspicious Order Quantities


I wanted to advise all of you that we re working with Security and the DEA Compliance Group (Bill Ratliff and Karen Harper) to develop procedures to insure we maintain compliance with the DEA requirement that we report any suspicious order quantities and/or patterns to them.   In light of the recent developments with McKesson, a good deal of focus is being placed on this project.

Briefly, if an order is deemed  peculiar  by a customer service rep based on a set of guidelines currently being developed, it will be placed on hold and the DEA compliance group (Bill Ratliff and Karen Harper) will be advised.  DEA Compliance will then conduct a more in-depth investigation and determine if the situation warrants notification to the DEA.  If the order is deemed appropriate, customer service will be notified and the order will be released from hold status for shipment.   If the outcome of the investigation supports that the order is in fact   suspicious  it will not be shipped and the local DEA office will be notified.   I would expect that we also develop a means of communication to the business group any time an order is placed on hold for reasons of peculiarity by the Customer Service Group.   Updates regarding the status of specific orders should be forwarded as well as the  peculiar order  proceeds through the review process.

Preliminary processes are in development and I m in the process of determining/evaluating how best to identify deviations from the norm based on the type of businesses we service as well as the products being purchased.  Criteria that is well suited for an AT Clinic may be too stringent for a Distributor.  Each class of customer (clinics, distributors, wholesalers, etc.) will be handled based on the merits of the business segment they support.  Any anomalies that support what we term as a  peculiar  order will be forwarded to the DEA compliance group for further investigation prior to it being turned over to the DEA.

As these respective formulas are developed, I will share them with you along with a sampling of data used to support the validity/effectiveness of the assumptions used in developing same.   At first pass, the formula might look like this:

-        Customers will be separated into their respective class of business (distributors, wholesalers, clinic, hospitals, retail, etc)

-        Add purchase quantities, by product (all Oxy products and again by individual skus) for the last 12 months for all customers within the same class of business for any controlled substances

o      Customer s with multiple  ship to  locations should have their total aggregated at the  sold to  level; but also reviewed at the  ship to  level

-        Add customer months for every record used in the above total (months within the last 12 that customer purchases of the item were not zero)

-        Divide total quantity purchases by the total customer months

-        Then multiply by the factor below to give the maximum mount that the customer can order per month before showing up on the suspicious order report.

o      Factor = 2 for C-II Controlled Substances

o      Factor = 4 for C-III, IV and V

Once the myriad aspects of this project are refined, selective excess order quantity business rules may require adjustment.

In addition to order quantities by product, we hope to also develop criteria for orders that deviate from normal ordering patterns and/or from usual order frequency (not yet sure how to capture this; hope to identify an algorithm that will support parsing through the data to identify patterns, frequency, etc.)  A report will be generated daily (at a minimum) but hope to eventually have the systems in place so customer service receives a  real time  flag when an order violates one of our parameters and will flag the order as peculiar.

The group is working on other indicators that might be used in evaluating whether or not a customer should be reported as  peculiar .  The Sales force will play a key role in this process by verifying the customer s physical site and operations ring true with the type of business they purport to run.  The DEA Compliance group is in the process of discussing this aspect with management on the Sales side of the business.

If you have any questions, please let me know.  This process is in preliminary stages so we may not have answers to all the questions that may come up, but those questions might also be food for thought in furthering the breadth of this project.

Regards,

Subject:Peculiar Orders
I just had a meeting with the CDIG group and as we discussed our relationship, how their systems work
and what their systems manage, we may have stumbled across something that should be considered as
part of our Peculiar Orders process.
Apparently over the course of a company s life, different aspects of the information associated with their
DEA license registration will change, i.e., they move to a different location; they change their name; they
change owners. Conceivably there could be a company that s been around for 50 years doing business for
us but if they move, CDIG sets them up with a new customer number so they appear to be a new
customer. I would think it would benefit our regulatory stewardship to be able to maintain the genealogy
of a specific company over the lifetime of their business with us. This would aid a new CSR in knowing
that this is a customer with whom we ve had a long lasting relationship but could also be a red flag of a
company who s in trouble financially and is trying to fly under the radar by moving frequently or changing
their name a lot. We simply update a customer record and add an  effective date  for  each change to the
record to create the links through all of the identities under which a company has done business and/or
locations at which this company may have operated. To have the ability to do this, we d have to
incorporate a change to the CDIG files to add the  affectivity date  for maintain historical information on
the customers.

Best Regards,

Thanks Lisa.

These orders hit the "threshold limit". I will probably butcher this, but here goes:

The report is looking at the previous 18 months of orders (product specific) for an average. It is them
multiplied by 3. this is called the "target average qty", which is an acceptable amou nt. Keep in mind
they are measured by molecule of the product family and not on skus.
The "target average qty" for hydromorphone is 106, actual order qty is 149 (again this is measured by
molecule)
The "target average qty" for morphine is 960, actual order qty is 1392 (molecules again)

This is not a very technical way of describing the process, but it is how I understand it.

This is just one of several formulas used on the report.

Hope this helps.

DEA Compliance Procedure   No:
Subject:  Revision No.:
 Draft 4 Published 07/15/08
Identification and Review of Peculiar Orders  Effective Date:

Controlled Substance Suspicious Order Monitoring Program  Supersedes Date:
NEW
 Page No.:
1  of 4

Originator: Security:
Karen Harper
Corporate Logistic  Documentation Coordinator:


PURPOSE:
This procedure formally outlines the internal criteria and standards to identify, capture,
investigate, report suspicious orders to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) prior to
shipment.
SCOPE:
Applies internally to Covidien Customer Service Group, Information Services Group, DEA
Compliance, and Security for monitoring of controlled substance orders received electronically
or manually, bulk or finished dosage products, for all active customer accounts from order
placement to shipment.
REFERENCES:
_  Title 21 CFR 1301.74(b)
The registrant shall design and operate a system to disclose to the registrant suspicio us orders of
controlled substances. The registrant shall inform the Field Division Office of the Administration
in his area of suspicious orders when discovered by the registrant. Suspicious orders include
orders of unusual size, orders deviating substantially from a normal pattern, and orders of
unusual frequency.
OVERVIEW:
DEA cannot/will not tell a DEA registrant if an order is legitimate and/or if an order should be
shipped.  It is fundamental for sound operations that DEA registrants take reasonable measures
to identify their customers, understand the normal and expected transactions typically conducted
by those customers, and, consequently identify those transactions that are suspicious in nature.
The Procedure for Identification and Review of Peculiar  Orders, Suspicious  Order Monitoring
Program, is designed for compliance by developing systems to:
 Identify, capture, and hold orders that meet Peculiar Order criteria


   QSP 00.00  Rev  TITLE  2  of 4

Investigate Peculiar Orders and release for shipment if authorized after review by
Security and DEA Compliance
Elevate  Peculiar Orders to the level of Suspicious Order based upon investigation
results and notify DEA   [per CFR21 1301.74(b)].
DEFINITIONS:
Peculiar Order   A controlled substance order that meets an internal, established criteri a
that will be placed on hold  pending further review by DEA Compliance.
Suspicious Order  A Peculiar Order that has been reviewed by DEA Compliance and
Security  and has been elevated to DEA reporting status.
REPORTS REQUIRED
_  Do Not Ship List
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Customer Service Representative
Perform the following activities for each controlled substance order:
1. Verify that the account is in good standing
 a. Reference the  Do Not Ship List  file on the Shared Drive.
2. Assure that the order is valid
 a.  Verify that the customer has provided a complete order
3. Check customer DEA registration status
 a. Current customer DEA registration certificate is to be on file  in Customer
  Service department
 b. DEA registration suspension/revocations can be checked by calling DEA
  Compliance group who will refer to DEA webpage, Registration Validation
  Link
4. For CI and CII controlled substance orders
 a. Verify customer has provided a DEA 222 form
b. Obtain a  Certificate of Available Procurement Quota  fro m customers using a
Manufacturing registration DEA 222 Form
c. Obtain a  Statement of Intended Use  from customers using a Research,
Compounding Pharmacy, or Analytical Lab registration DEA 222 Form
 I. Forward the  Statement of Intended Use  to DEA Compliance
5. Review the order based on the criteria above and identify order as  Peculiar  if there are
any exceptions
6. Forward  Peculiar  order information to Customer Service Manager and Security
Director

Customer Service Manager


   QSP 00.00  Rev  TITLE  3  of 4


1.  Review the IS system  generated Peculiar Order Report which lists orders that meet the
criteria established in this procedure
a. Annotate the report with applicable explanation that authorizes shipment of
Peculiar Orders that deviates from normal order pattern, size, frequency such as
trade show sales, etc.
b. Manually release orders in the order entry system that are authorized to  ship
c.. For orders that have no applicable explanation for deviation from normal order
pattern, size, frequency, the order will remain on hold pending further
investigation by the business group and Security/DEA Compliance.
d.. Upon completion of review, forward the annotated Peculiar Order  Report to
Security/DEA Compliance for record retention per Company policy
2. Maintains  the Do Not Ship List on the Shared drive by updating for any customer for
which shipment has been cancelled based on suspicious order criteria.


Information Service Department


1.  Programs and publishes the order entry generated Peculiar Order Report which lists
orders that  meet the criteria as follows:
a.  Orders in excess of 2X the amount of product ordered during the previous fiscal
year andYTD average by customer, by sku.
b. Orders that appear on the Peculiar Order Report will be placed on hold
automatically within the order entry system
c. The Peculiar Order Report exempts orders from the 20? largest customers in each
customer category (Wholesalers, Distributors).


Security Director  and DEA Compliance
1. Investigates Peculiar Orders that have no applicable explanation for deviation from
normal order pattern, size, frequency
2. Consults with the business group as part of the Peculiar Order investigation
3. Reviews Peculiar Orders for correlation to  DEA webpage  Drugs of Concern Listing
4. Responsible for DEA reporting of orders that have been  escalated from Peculiar Order
status to Suspicious Order status
5. Maintains files of Peculiar Order Reports and Suspicious Order Investigation
documentation per Mallinckrodt/Covidien per Covidien Record Retention Policy
6. Responsible for training internal customers on this procedure.


  QSP 00.00  Rev  TITLE  4  of 4

DEA Compliance Procedure   No:
Subject:  Revision No.:
 Draft 3  published 06/02/08
Controlled Substance Suspicious Order Monitoring  Effective Date:

 Supersedes Date:
NEW
 Page No.:
1  of 5

Originator: Security:
Karen Harper
Corporate Logistics: Documentation Coordinator:


PURPOSE:
Establish a procedure to identify and report controlled substance suspicious orders  to the Drug
Enforcement Administration  (DEA) prior to shipment.  DEA cannot/will not tell a DEA
registrant if an order is legitimate and/or if an order should  be shipped. It is fundamental for
sound operations that DEA registrants take reasonable measures to identify their customers,
understand the normal and expected transactions typically  conducted by those customer, and,
consequently identify those transactions that are suspicious in nature. SCOPE:
Applies to establishing a new controlled substance customer account and subsequent shipment of
all controlled substance orders to new or established customers.
REFERENCES:
Title 21 CFR 1301.74(b)
The registrant shall design and operate a system to disclose to the registrant suspicious orders of
controlled substances. The registrant shall inform the Field Division Office of the Administration
in his area of suspicious orders when discovered by the registrant. Suspicious orders include
orders of unusual size, orders deviating substantially from a normal pattern, and o rders of
unusual frequency..
DEFINITIONS:
Peculiar Order   A controlled substance order that meets an  internal, established criteria
that will be placed on hold  pending further review by DEA Compliance.
Suspicious Order  A Peculiar Order that has been reviewed by DEA Compliance and
Security that will not be shipped and will be reported to the Drug
Enforcement Administration.


   QSP 00.00  Rev 1  TITLE  2  of 5


RESPONSIBILITIES:
Credit Department
Performs  Dun & Bradstreet  and/or other information checks  on new controlled substance
customers to determine credit worthiness.
Refers  the new customer account to Security Director or DEA Compliance if the new account
has no historical or financial information available or if the data shows liens, lawsuits, or other
information which might rais e suspicions as to the legitimacy of the new account company.
Conducts  periodic checks for existing accounts. Notifies Security Director or DEA Compliance
of any customer credit concerns.
Field Sales
Completes Site Survey Checklist for New Controlled Substance Customers (Attachment A)
Conducts an on-site visit including taking photographs inside and out for review  by Security
Director and DEA Compliance Manager.

Customer Service Representatives
Bulk Narcotics Customer  Service Representatives will  perform the following activities for each
order entered:
Verify that the customer has a valid DEA Registration certificate
Assure that the customer has provided a DEA 222 form for CI and CII substances
Obtain a  Certificate of Available Procurement Quota  from cus tomers using a Manufacturing
Registration DEA 222 Form
Obtain a  Statement of Intended Use  from customers using a Research or Analytical Lab
Registration DEA 222 Form  for quantities of >500 grams of material
Forward the  Statement of Intended Use  to DEA  Compliance for review
Designate an order as  Peculiar  if the customer fails to provide the appropriate documentation
above.
Forward Peculiar Order  information to Customer  Service Manager and Security Director

Dosage Customer Service Representatives will  perform the following activities for
_________________need clarification, orders for all new Retail or Wholesale accounts may be
reviewed, Retail Chain Pharmacies may be exempted.
- Verify that the customer has a valid DEA registration certificate
- Insure the customer has provided a properly executed DEA 222 form for CI and
CII substances


   QSP 00.00  Rev 1  TITLE  3  of 5

- Flag orders that deviate from the norm in terms of quantity ordered, frequency of
order and/or pattern of normal order  placement, CSR s will evaluate the
circumstances of the order. This evaluation should be based on their knowledge
of the specific customer and the industry in which the customer operates  and
should the circumstances deviate from the norm, upon completi on of the order,
place same on hold and notify Security and the Customer Service Manager.
___________________

If Dosage Customer Service representatives are contacted by a new customer asking that an
account be set up  and the interview process yields questionable results, the CSR will obtain the
following information from the customer and forward the information in an e-mail to the
Director of Security (Bill Ratliff) as well as the Customer Service Manager. In addition to the
pedigree information listed below, the CSR should recap the circumstances of the conversation
which caused them to question the authenticity of the caller and/or business.
- Contact s name, address and phone
- Name of business
- Type of business
- DEA License number
Customer Service Manager
Obtains a Peculiar Order Daily Report from the order entry system  forwarded to a group mail
box  that highlights orders that are unusually large, unusually frequent, and/or deviating in
quantity from an established order pattern.

Annotates  the Peculiar Order Report if there is a valid business reason for an order of unusually
large, unusually frequent, and/or deviating in quantity from an established order pattern.
Forward the Peculiar Order Report to Security Director/DEA Compliance.

Customer Service Manager will maintain a  Do Not Ship List  of customers to whom Covidien
has ceased distribution due to suspicious activity.

For Bulk Narcotics, an order will be deemed to be Peculiar if the order quantity is double the
amount of product ordered during the previous fiscal year and YTD average by sku, by
customer.

For Dosage Narcotics, an order will be deemed to be Peculiar if the order quantity exceeds the
result of a formula based on the class of business in which the business operates  (AT clinics,
distributors, wholesalers, hospitals, retailers, etc).  This is only until such time as we re able to
develop a method for the system to flag these orders real time    .???

- Proposed  Preliminary  Dosage Formula:


   QSP 00.00  Rev 1  TITLE  4  of 5

- Add purchase quantities, by product (all Oxy products and again by individual
skus) for the last 12 months for all customers within the same class of business for any
controlled substances
o  Customer s with multiple  ship to  locations should have their total
aggregated at the  sold to  level; but also reviewed at the  ship to  level
- Add customer months for every record used in the above total (months within
the last 12 that customer purchases of the item were not zero)
- Divide total quantity purchases by the total customer months
- Then multiply by the factor below to give the maximum mount that the
customer can order per month before showing up on the suspicious order
report.
o  Factor = 2 for C-II Controlled Substances
o  Factor = 4 for C-III, IV and V
These factors will vary depending on the business   we ll need to figure this out.
Retail chain pharmacies may be exempted

- Formula for AT Clinics
- Formula for Distributors  -
- Formula for Wholesalers
- Formula for ??
- Formula for ??  ______ ______

____________________________________________________________
________________________________________________________________________


Upon receipt of notification from the Director of Security that a specific order or customer has
been deemed Peculiar, the Customer Service Manager will forward notification to the
appropriate business director, manager and sales representative.


Security Director  and DEA Compliance
Provides blank Site Survey Checklist forms for New Controlled Substance Customers to be
completed by Field Sales
Reviews results of Site Survey Checklist for New Controlled Substance Customers and provides
authorization to proceed with new customer account set-up
Determines if Peculiar Orders are to be shipped or designated as Suspicious Orders and not
shipped  based upon information received from the Credit Department, Customer Service, Field


  QSP 00.00  Rev 1  TITLE  5  of 5

Sales, and DEA Webpage  Drugs of Concern Listing .  Notifies Customer Service of final
decision on each peculiar and/or suspicious order/customer.

Maintains a file for record retention of Suspicious Order Monitoring documents and reports
per Covidien Record Retention Policy.

Conducts training on the Controlled Substance Suspicious Order Monitoring Procedure for
Credit Department, Field Sales, and Customer Service.

text:
Global Controlled Substance Compliance
 No. C/S Comp 3.0
 Procedure
Subject:  Revision Date:
Identification and Review of Peculiar Orders  03/28/11
Mallinckrodt Controlled Substance Suspicious Order Monitoring
Program

Originator: Page 1 of 4
Karen Harper
Senior Manager, Controlled Substance Compliance


PURPOSE:
In accordance with U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) regulations 21 CFR
1301.74(b), Mallinckrodt has an obligation to inform DEA of suspicious orders.
This procedure outlines the Identification and Review of Peculiar Orders component o f the
Mallinckrodt Suspicious Order Monitoring Program.
APPLIES TO:
Controlled Substance Customer Service Representatives and Managers
Information Service Group
Finance &Administration
Suspicious Order Monitoring Leadership Team
Commercial Group
Controlled Substance Compliance
Security  Director
OVERVIEW:
DEA communication to industry assigns shared responsibility for maintaining appropriate
safeguards against diversion to all registrants.
The Mallinckrodt Controlled Substance Procedure for Identification and Review of Peculiar
Orders, Suspicious  Order Monitoring Program, is designed to:
Define the internal criteria for detecting Peculiar Orders that require further review
Elevate  Peculiar Orders to the level of Suspicious Order as needed, based upon
investigation results, and notification to  DEA  accordingly


   C/S Comp  Identification and Review of Peculiar Orders  2  of 5
3.0  Controlled Substance Compliance Suspicious Order Monitoring Program

DEFINITIONS:
Peculiar Order:  Mallinckrodt direct customer controlled substance order that meets an
internal, established criteria  of 3X the average amount of product ordered
during the previous 12  months by DEA reporting class

Suspicious Order  A Peculiar Order that has been investigated by Finance, Security  Director,
Controlled Substance Compliance without resolution and is elevated to
DEA reportable status
REPORTS REQUIRED
_  Peculiar Order Report
_  Returned 222 Excel Spreadsheet
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Customer Service Representative
Perform the following activities for each controlled substance order:
1. Verify that the account is in good standing  by reviewing the  Do Not Ship List  file on
the Shared Drive

2. Assure that the order is valid  by completing an evaluation and verification of an order to
determine  that the customer has provided a complete order

3. For CI and CII controlled substance orders
 a. Verify customer has provided a complete DEA 222 form
b. Confirm that DEA 222 Purchaser address agrees with customer DEA registration
license
 c. Review the DEA 222 form for any unusual entries  or anomalies
d. Return the 222 form to the customer if it is unacceptable, enter returned 222
information in the  Returned 222 Excel Spreadsheet report
e. Forwards the Returned 222 Excel spreadsheet to Controlled Substance
Compliance monthly
f. Obtain a  Certificate of Available Procurement Quota  from bulk API  customers
using a Manufacturing Registration DEA 222 Form
g  Obtain a  Statement of Intended Use  from customers using a Research,
Compounding Pharmacy, or Analytical Lab registration DEA 222 Form

4. Review the order based on the criteria above and  refer to Controlled Substance
Compliance for additional inve stigation as required

Information Services Department


   C/S Comp  Identification and Review of Peculiar Orders  3  of 5
3.0  Controlled Substance Compliance Suspicious Order Monitoring Program


1.  Programs and publishes the Peculiar Order Report which lists dosage and API orders that
meet the criteria as follows:
a.  Orders in excess of 3X the average amount of product ordered during the previous
12 months  by customer, by DEA reporting class. The algorithms have been
established to identify whether a customer is deviating from a normal order
pattern, and/or increasing in frequency


Finance & Adminstration

1.  Review the IS system generated Peculiar Order Report which lists orders that meet the
established criteria

2.  Annotate Peculiar Order Report accordingly if Finance & Administration review
authorizes shipment with no further investigation, include signature and date reference for
notations

 2a. At the written direction of the Suspicious Order Monitoring Leadership Team,
Peculiar Order investigation is adjusted to address individual
product/order/customer circumstances as needed based upon specific diversion
trends
3a. If input from Commercial Group is required  in the course of Finance &
Administration Peculiar Order review, obtain documentation from Commercial
Group in support of review conclusion

3. Maintains files of Peculiar Order reports and investigation findings for those Pec uliar
Orders that do not require further investigation

1. Refer Peculiar Orders that warrant further investigation to Controlled Substance
Compliance or Security  Director

Commercial Group

Responds to Finance & Administration Group inquiries related to Pec uliar Order Report
investigation. Responses may include recommendations to approve Peculiar Orders for shipment
based upon market knowledge such as receipt of new customer supply agreements or other
justification

Suspicious Order Monitoring Leadership Team

1. Collaborates with Security and Controlled Substance Compliance to adjust Peculiar
Order review based on diversion trends
2.
Consults with Security and Compliance in Monthly Meetings to provide oversight and
guidance for all aspects of the Suspicious Order Monitoring Program


   C/S Comp  Identification and Review of Peculiar Orders  4  of 5
3.0  Controlled Substance Compliance Suspicious Order Monitoring Program


Controlled Substance Compliance

1. Investigates  Peculiar Orders that have no applicable explanation for deviation from
normal order pattern, size, and frequency, in conjunction with Security Director  upon
referral from Finance & Administration

2. Consults with the Commercial Group  as part of the peculiar order investigation, in
conjunction with Security Director

3. Reviews Peculiar Orders for comparison to DEA webpage  Drugs of Concern Listing ,
in conjunction with Security Director

4. Responsible for reporting to DEA Peculiar Orders that have been investigated and further
defined as Suspicious Orders, in conjunction with Security Director

5. Maintains files of Peculiar Order reports and investigation findings for those Peculia r
Orders that have required further investigation, in conjunction with Security Director

6. Responsible for training internal customers on this procedure, in  conjunction with
Security Director

7. In conjunction with Security, responsible for training internal  stakeholders on this
procedure

Security Director
1. Investigates  Peculiar Orders that have no applicable explanation for deviation from
normal order pattern, size, and frequency, in conjunction with Controlled Substance
Compliance

2. Consults with the  Commercial Group as part of the peculiar order investigation, in
conjunction with Controlled Substance Compliance

3. Reviews Peculiar Orders for comparison to DEA webpage  Drugs of Concern Listing ,
in conjunction with Controlled Substance Compliance

4. Responsible for reporting to DEA Peculiar Orders that have been investigated and further
defined as Suspicious Orders, in conjunction with Controlled Substance Compliance

5. Maintains files of Peculiar Order reports and investigation findings for those Peculiar
Orders that have required further investigation, in conjunction with Controlled Substance
Compliance


  C/S Comp  Identification and Review of Peculiar Orders  5  of 5
3.0  Controlled Substance Compliance Suspicious Order Monitoring Program


6. Responsible for training internal customers on this procedure  in, conjunction with
Controlled Substance Compliance


7
In conjunction with Controlled Substance Compliance, responsible for training internal
stakeholders on this procedure

Revision History

03/29/11
Added Revision History section to  document future changes to this procedure

Subject: Oct 2013 AMCP Activities: Meeting Notes



 

All,

 

Thank you for a very productive meeting.  As usual we had a thoughtful discussion and landed on a strong framework for the Oct AMCP meeting and foundation on AD positioning for the KAD/MSL deck to support the launch

 

Following are action items and meeting minutes:

 

Attendees:

J. Decker, J. Patrick, D. Hasse, C. Kisinger, J. Duarte, L. Saake

 

Action Items:

·        Determine if we can do an ADT Theater at October meeting – Connie & Joe

·        Contact AMCP to determine if there is an opportunity to submit – Late Breaking Trial abstracts (possibly to leverage HAL data?) – Connie & Joe

·        Contact AMCP to understand if we can conduct an ADT Theater  – Connie & Joe

·        Contact AMCP to understand timing and conditions for proposal/abstract submissions for Spring 2013 meeting (submission date Oct 2013) -  John?

·        Provide to John potential MCO thought leaders for inclusion at the MSA-HAL Ad Board and interest in attendance by marketing & PriceSpectives – Connie & Joe

·        Schedule a working meeting at end of June of key stakeholders/contributors to developing the ADT Theater content; also frame work for ADT content for KAD & MSL discussions with payers – Leah Paul

 

Meeting Minutes:

 

1.       Joe summarized the need to understand/finalize position on the viability of MNK795 data and MC needs:

·        Organization Ask is to get Tier 2 status.  To accomplish this Access Marketing/Sales needs:

o   Comparative effectiveness trials that show superiority to Percocet (efficacy & AD)

o   Advocacy and Policy (2-3 years to get up)

o   This will not be available at launch; we must determine how to leverage the data we have and additional information/levers in the public domain

o   Utilize Payer Ad Board  at AMCP to understand how we can leverage the data we have, augmented with supporting information in the public domain and evaluate the LCM studies currently being scoped

 

2.       Draft Agenda – October AMCP Meeting

·        Package of Information:  OC change in formulation resulted in EPI change

·        Vicodin re-scheduling

·        Independent states – not waiting for Federal legislation

·        FDA guidance ADT

·        Political/Societal movement in support of ADT

·        Implications to future approval of opioid medications (Zogenix)

·        Types/Bars for abuse:  Physio-mechanical manipulation,  injection, snorting,  oral use (highest risk group from payer perspective?)

·        Is there an analysis that demonstrates the implications of the above – can we identify physicians/treatments/pills per procedures/pain condition

Game Changer:  With the introduction of our formulation, the “Race to Powder” doesn’t win (crushing and tampering) – Moves to “ Race to Cmax/Tmax” - MNK795 AD strength

·        Working meeting about current data analysis about the problem; what additional data is in public domain that support/supplements our data – create unmet need

3.      Working Group:  J. Duarte, C. Kisinger, PriceSpectives (CK to provide attendees), J. Patrick, J. Decker, J. Anderson, A. Pennell,  C. Burton &/or B. Franco; consider including Cliff Herman (MNK795 lead formulator) & Krishna Devarakonda (PK specialists)

 

4.        October 2013 Meeting:

·        Missed abstract/poster opportunity for the Oct meeting?  Is there a chance for late breaking/encore?  Maggie Glassman investigating. AI – meeting will be scheduled to discuss specifically

·        There is not booth presence at meeting

·        Could we do an ADT Theater – hosted by Medical Affairs & post reception?

·        MNK795 Ad Board is planned (separate from the conference) – Connie, Joe & PriceSpectives are developing plan and tactical execution

·        Reception is planned all-comers – being scoped:  PriceSpectives will be driving this.  Goal is present One Mallinckrodt; possibility to expand to AD if late breaking/encore material is allowed

 

5.       Spring 2014 Meeting:

·        Spring 2014 Mtg for proposal and abstract submission is Oct 25 2013.

 

 

6.       JMPC Opportunities:

·        Lisa reported that JMCP has a call for information on articles on many aspects of  Pain Management – Phil Linder from JMPC next week; this will be discussed

From: Morelli, Art

Subject: RE: Exalgo REMS Information Request


 

Hi Maria et al,

 

Thanks for the questions. I am so glad the MSL team is engaged in, and thinking about, REMS, and the specifics of the safe and appropriate use of our products, especially Exalgo. It is clear to me that we can be a leader in this area( Leading the Science of Safety), but only with the kind of "best in class" MSL team that is currently being formed. This leadership, first in REMS and soon after in an even broader and deeper safe use initiative( the CARES Alliance) will help differentiate us as a company that both knows and does what is right.

 

Please find the answers below:

 

1) The physician call list for Exalgo could include "prescription mills". When we determine that this is the case for a particular call point, Med Affairs will address this with Commercial to take the most appropriate steps. As you can imagine, there is a range of responses we could take depending on the details. Clearly, we are dedicated to mitigating abuse, misuse,overdose, and addiction( risks named in our REMS), and diversion( not named in our REMS). We will do whatever we can to help solve these problems. We could become aware of this from Sales Rep reports or from very unusual Rx activity which we monitor.

 

2) We receive weekly reports of Rx data( about a 2 week lag), and the identity of prescribers( about a 3 week lag). Less frequently we receive very detailed reports on the longitudinal Rx activity by physician name, by patient de-identified. This includes the script size, strength, and the patient's previous opioid therapy in detail (key for assessing prior opioid tolerance in patients starting Exalgo). We will marry this data to our list of physicians who have completed the Exalgo prescriber education.

 

3) Yes, we will collect trends and correlations, and they will be reviewed approximately monthly by our internal oversight group, the CAC( Covidien Assessment Committee), and then presented to our RSAB( REMS Safety Advisory Board) twice a year. This is an external team of external experts in epidemiology, pain management, REMS , education, etc. Lynn Webster is the Chair. The first meeting of the RSAB will be in late Sept in St Louis. The timing correlates with our Exalgo REMS assessments that go to the FDA.

 

4) We distributed via first class mail just before launch the Exalgo Healthcare Professional Education Kit to the following targets:

 

a) all retail and hospital pharmacies in the US which is over 70 k recipients. This was not required by the FDA amazingly enough.

b) all professional pharmacy associations and Boards. Also not required.

c) the 20 k prescribers in our commercial call plan( required by the FDA).

d) an additional 40 k prescribers not in our call plan but whom prescribe LAO's.( not required by the FDA).

e) all relevant physician  professional associations and Boards.( required).

 

5) The kit contains the following elements:

 

a) Dear HCP letter from Herb that explains the REMS and discusses Exalgo( PI with Med Guide is attached).

b) Prescribing Brochure with another PI and Med Guide attached. The brochure discusses general opioid use and risks, Exalgo risks, and recommended approaches to mitigate these risks.

c) The EEIF form for the HCP to submit to document that they reviewed the Prescribing Brochure.

d) These 3 pieces are in a portfolio that explains what to do and contains contact information for www.exalgorems.com and our Call Center.

e) A BRC to request two initial tools from the CARES Alliance: 1) the APS Tx Guidelines Reprint and 2) the widely acclaimed Scott Fishman, MD text on Safe and Appropriate Use of Opioids.

 

Our Sales Force has an allocation of these materials and directions to request additional materials via an automated system.

INDICATION

EXALGO(r) (hydromorphone HCI) Extended-Release Tablets (CII) is indicated for the management of moderate to severe pain in opioid tolerant patients requiring continuous, around-the-clock opioid analgesia for an extended period of time.

IMPORTANT RISK INFORMATION

WARNING: POTENTIAL FOR ABUSE, IMPORTANCE OF PROPER PATIENT SELECTION AND LIMITATIONS OF USE


Abuse Potential

EXALGO contains hydromorphone, an opioid agonist and a Schedule II controlled substance with an abuse liability similar to other opioid agonists, legal or illicit. Assess each patient's risk for opioid abuse or addiction prior to prescribing EXALGO. The risk for opioid abuse is increased in patients with a personal or family history of substance abuse (including drug or alcohol abuse or addiction) or mental illness (e.g., major depressive disorder). Routinely monitor all patients receiving EXALGO for signs of misuse, abuse, and addiction during treatment.

Life-threatening Respiratory Depression

Respiratory depression, including fatal cases, may occur with use of EXALGO, even when the drug has been used as recommended and not misused or abused. EXALGO is for use in opioid tolerant patients only. Proper dosing and titration are essential and EXALGO should be prescribed only by healthcare professionals who are knowledgeable in the use of potent opioids for the management of chronic pain. Monitor for respiratory depression, especially during initiation of EXALGO or following a dose increase. Crushing, dissolving, or chewing the tablet can cause rapid release and absorption of a potentially fatal dose of hydromorphone.

Accidental Exposure

Accidental ingestion of EXALGO, especially in children, can result in a fatal overdose of hydromorphone.


*

EXALGO is contraindicated in:



-

Opioid non-tolerant patients. Fatal respiratory depression could occur in patients who are not opioid tolerant.

-

Patients with significant respiratory depression

-

Patients with acute or severe bronchial asthma in an unmonitored setting or in the absence of resuscitative equipment

-

Patients with known or suspected paralytic ileus

-

Patients who have had surgical procedures and/or underlying disease resulting in narrowing of the gastrointestinal tract, or have "blind loops" of the gastrointestinal tract or gastrointestinal obstruction

-

Patients with hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to hydromorphone or sulfite-containing medications


*

EXALGO is indicated for opioid tolerant patients only. Patients considered opioid tolerant are those who are taking at least 60 mg oral morphine per day, 25 mcg transdermal fentanyl/hour, 30 mg oral oxycodone/day, 8 mg oral hydromorphone/day, 25 mg oral oxymorphone/day or an equianalgesic dose of another opioid, for a week or longer.

*

EXALGO is not intended for use as an as-needed analgesic and is not indicated for the management of acute or postoperative pain. It is contraindicated in patients who need management of mild pain or pain not expected to persist.

*

Avoid concurrent use of alcohol and EXALGO. Concurrent use of EXALGO with CNS depressants, including alcohol, increases risk of respiratory depression, hypotension, and profound sedation, potentially resulting in coma or death. EXALGO may impair the ability to drive a car or operate machinery.

*

Not intended in patients who have received MAO inhibitors within 14 days of starting EXALGO.

*

Use with caution and in reduced doses in older or debilitated patients, as well as patients with renal or hepatic insufficiency, Addison's disease, delirium tremens, myxedema or hypothyroidism, prostatic hypertrophy or urethral stricture, toxic psychosis. May aggravate convulsions in patients with convulsive disorders; may induce or aggravate seizures in some clinical settings. Consider use of an alternate analgesic in patients with severe renal impairment.

*

Respiratory depression, which occurs more frequently in elderly or debilitated patients, is the chief hazard with EXALGO.

*

Serious adverse events could also include hypotensive effects, GI effects, cardiac arrest from overdose and precipitation of withdrawal. Most common adverse events (>10%) seen in clinical studies (N=2474) were: constipation (31%), nausea (28%), vomiting, somnolence, headache, asthenia and dizziness.

*

Use EXALGO with extreme caution in patients susceptible to intracranial effects of CO2 retention.

*

Do not abruptly discontinue EXALGO.

Hi BJ,

 

Hope all is well.

 

Since you were not able to be there in person today, I wanted to give
you my perspective on the day. Overall take away: we are on to something
unique and innovative in this space.

 

First and foremost, all of what I am going to relate was made possible
by Bill's strong relationships in the account, meeting prep, logistical
execution and strategic account planning. As we both know, when all
these things are in place, the execution flows and we look good.

 

The presentation was in 4 basic parts:

 

1)     Bill nicely set it up, provided an overview of the agenda and
framed the approach we were about to take ( 5 min).

2)     Karrie provided a very succinct overview of Exalgo pharmacology
with appropriate emphasis on aspects relevant to this audience: e.g.
true QD, CYP insights, rationale for opioid rotation, dose dumping,
co-morbidities. Her presentation separated validity from relevance very
well. She handled questions with aplomb. ( about 25 mins)

3)     I presented the Exalgo REMS, the Exalgo REMS performance data,
and a CARES Alliance review. This was not REMSology 101, but an inside
view of REMS operations, and how we could work together to enhance
appropriate prescribing and safe use among their member prescribers and
patients. We also pitched some unique collaborative projects we can
discuss later.( 25 mins). Preston created a new deck and it is strong.

weeks leading to the meeting: Medimpact believes they have sufficient
opioids( LAO's and IR's) on their formulary to adequately treat pain,

this Karrie emphasized that the rotation of tolerant patients does not
mean more opioid use, it promises better analgesia and/or fewer AEs.

solution, not part of the societal problem, and we are working to keep

Dear Gene,

 

As you advised, the JDC had approved submission of the REMS on Monday, November 2, and the documents were sent to the agency and are now under active review.  We have reviewed the additional changes forwarded by Stu Kim and have the following observations:

 

·         In general, the changes are inconsistent with labeling, the REMS Supporting Document, and FDA advice on the REMS.

·         The goals of the REMS were dictated by the FDA in their advice letter, and are the same as Embeda, and we note that these have changed.

·         The changes to the REMS do not match the REMS supporting document.

·         The FDA’s advice was to remove promotional language in the HCP letters such as “pleased to announce” and this has been re-inserted into the text.

·         The FDA’s advice was to include the full indication in the HCP letters, and this has been truncated in the revised versions.

·         The revised letters contain a black box, which does not match the warnings in the black box, and would not be accepted by FDA.  Additionally, FDA specifically advised that text boxes not be used to highlight specific information as it minimizes the importance of other information in the letter, and minimizes the REMS risks associated with EXALGO.

·         The HCP letters contain language which is inconsistent with the label.

·         The track changes files do not match the versions submitted in the NDA, thus, we cannot use these files as presented.

·         The “clean” versions of the files contain substantial formatting changes relative to the track changes version, and are not entirely accurate, e.g., the toll free phone number on REMS disappears in the clean version so these are not direct ‘accept changes’ versions.

·         There are a large number of editorial changes which would require a new FDA review of the entire REMS.

 

We recommend to the JDC that we maintain the current REMS text as submitted on Monday (11/2/09).

Dear Lisa,

Please find attached the EXALGO Medication Guide with the FDA changes accepted. 

 

The only additional comment is to propose to add back under  Before taking EXALGO, tell your healthcare provider if you have a history of:  a bullet for  allergy to sulfites .  The rationale being that, although the chance of exposure to sulfites from the use of metabisulfite in the synthesis of the active ingredient, hydromorphone HCl, in EXALGO is minimal and acknowledging that metabisulfite is not an excipient used in the formulation of in EXALGO extended-release tablets, since  sulfite allergy  is included as a Contraindication and under Warnings and Precautions in the EXALGO PI and since patients are generally aware of an allergy to sulfites, it should be included in the Medication Guide.

 

As additional rationale, the following are excerpts from the CVS Pharmacy Health Information Center website article  Could You Be Allergic to Sulfites? . 

 

http://health.cvs.com/GetContent.aspx?token=f75979d3-9c7c-4b16-af56-3e122a3f19e3&chunkiid=644494

 

What Is Sulfite Sensitivity?


You are considered to be sensitive to sulfites if you have an allergic reaction after consuming or applying this preservative. The symptoms, which range from mild to severe, can include:

         Skin problems itchy skin, rash, hives

         Digestive problems stomach cramps, nausea, diarrhea

         Respiratory problems wheezing, cough, difficulty breathing, tightness in the chest

In extreme situations, a life-threatening allergic reaction called anaphylactic shock may occur, where the person is not able to breath and experiences a drop in blood pressure.

How common is this sensitivity? Actually, the FDA estimates that the number of Americans who are allergic to sulfites is low. But people with asthma seem to have a higher risk of experiencing a reaction to these chemicals.

 

Check Your Medication

Sulfites are added to many prescription and over-the-counter medications. Surprisingly, this preservative is often found in drugs used to treat asthma and allergies. Other types of medications that may have sulfites include:

         Drugs to treat vomiting and nausea

         Cardiovascular medicines

         Antibiotics

         Psychotropic drugs

         Medications delivered by IV

         Pain relievers

         Anesthetics

         Steroids and other medications to help with respiratory problems

Read the drug label carefully. If you have any questions, talk to your doctor and pharmacist.

 

Mallinckrodt is accepting of all the other FDA changes to the EXALGO Medication Guide.

Linda

Research Update

 
Mallinckrodt plc

 
This morning, Mallinckrodt announced a three year distribution agreement with Amneal (private) on generic Suboxone (for the maintenance treatment of opioid dependence) sublingual tablets. Terms of the deal were not disclosed. While we don t believe this announcement will have a material impact to our estimates, the much larger market opportunity is tied to Reckitt Benckiser s Suboxone sublingual film, which we estimate has annual sales in excess of $1 billion. We believe the market opportunity with Suboxone sublingual tablets is much smaller (~$70-$75 million), with two generic players (Actavis and Amneal). According to Source Healthcare Analytics prescription data, as of the end of July, Actavis and Amneal each held a 45-47% share in the Suboxone tablet market, with Reckitt Benckiser s branded product holding the remaining share. Our analysis of the prescription market suggests that Reckitt has effectively transferred approximately 85% of Suboxone prescriptions over to its sublingual film.

 

Between now and year-end, we think investors will focus on three upcoming events; 1) the potential release of additional details on MNK-795 (an abuse deterrent formulation of an acetaminophen/opioid combination product) at the upcoming Pain Week Medical Conference in Las Vegas, NV on September 4-7, 2) the Company s planned release of F 14 financial guidance by the end of October, and 3) an FDA decision on the approvability of MNK-795 potentially by year end. Our F 14-F 16 estimates include MNK-795 revenues of $25 million, $75 million, and $120 million, respectively.

 

Investment Summary   SELL/$34PT. We maintain our SELL rating and $34PT, which we arrive at via a 7.1x multiple on our 2013 EBITDA estimate of $382 million, and a P/E multiple (11.6x our CY13 EPS estimate of $2.92). MNK shares currently trade at 14.7x our CY13 EPS estimate of $2.92, and 18.8x our CY14 EPS estimate of $2.28. On average, we believe MNK shares are trading at a 53% premium to its peers on a forward P/E multiple basis. Based on our expectations for MNK to face additional competition on several of its key pharmaceutical products (generic Concerta, and Exalgo) in the second half of 2013, we believe F 14 revenue could fall approximately (4.6%) vs. F 13, with EPS dropping to $2.27 (21% YOY) in F 14. With F 14 expected to be a transition year, we believe MNK shares could drop 23% from current levels.

Cc: "Mannebach, Mark" <mark.mannebach@mallinckrodt.com>,
    "Smith, Thomas" <thomas.smith@mallinckrodt.com>


Dear All,

We have received a similar comment from Dr. Henry Richards at Janssen in regard to the FDA proposed 4-mg increments for dose escalations of EXALGO (please see below forwarded email from Tamara).

 

Since the proposed 4-mg incremental increase seems to be the only issue that we would be pushing back on, could the team please help with phrasing the rationale to be included in our response to the FDA changes for the class labeling.  Acknowledging that we might want to be more brief in our response, my initial draft from comments received in emails from the team is the following:

 

The 4?mg dose increment is problematic from a prescription/patient instructions-logistics perspective, creating prescribing issues for physicians and safety issues for patients.  The concerns with this prescriptive approach are that it would not only hinder appropriate management of the opioid-tolerant patient s pain but could also result in safety issues due to patient confusion and error when multiple tablet strengths were required to achieve a prescribed dose.  There is also the additional safety concern for patients splitting tablets to save money on the additional strength prescriptions.

 

If the aim is to label a specific mg incremental dose escalation, Mallinckrodt recommends an 8-mg a titrating dose for EXALGO and once stabilized on 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, etc., the patient could be converted to a regimen using fewer tablets.



This prescriptive approach is especially concerning combined with the removal of the proposed 25% dose reduction from previous opioid therapy, which was based on the EXALGO clinical trial (50% reductions were never studied). Drastic dose reductions in this opioid tolerant population could lead to repeat, i.e., over-dosing due to inadequacy of the first dose and the 4 days required to achieve steady state for EXALGO.  Similarly, the minimal 4-mg dose increment could increase the rates of withdrawal symptoms in the opioid-tolerant patients who would be prescribed EXALGO.

 

Also at issue is our proposed text for this statement in Highlights under Dosage and Administration, as well as the FDA addition to Section 2.2 Titration and Maintenance of Therapy, which is copied here:

 

Plasma levels of EXALGO are sustained for 18 to 24 hours. Dosage adjustments of EXALGO may be made in increments of 4 mg every 3 to 4 days as needed to achieve adequate analgesia.


 

Our previous suggestion for the Highlights section in response to the FDA request follows:

 

     Dose may be increased every 3 to 4 days as needed to achieve adequate analgesia[EF1] . If titration is needed, consider a 25% to 50% increase in the dose[Covidien2] . (2.2)

 

Do we want to go back to that original proposal or rather propose to substitute  8-mg  for the FDA proposed   4-mg  in both sections of the labeling?

 

     Dose may be increased using increments of 4 mg every 3 to 4 days as needed to achieve adequate analgesia[EF3] . (2.2)

 

Thanks for any comments.  And since a team meeting would likely be beneficial to finalize our comments for this draft labeling, we have reserved the room 435 on Thurs at 4pm Central time.

Kind regards,

Linda

I think the 4?mg dose increment is problematic from a prescription/patient instructions-logistics perspective.

Subject: Requested DocAlert: How Many Opioid Pills Are Your Patients Taking Each Day?
From: DocAlert <docalert@epocrates.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Mar 2013 10:30:17 -0600
To: Chelsey Homan <choman@epocrates.com>


Dear Clinician:

Here is the information you requested (sponsored by Mallinckrodt).

 

Once-Daily EXALGO  (hydromorphone HCl) Extended-Release Tablets (CII)

May Help Reduce Pill Burden

How many 20 mg or 40 mg pills are your OxyContin  (oxycodone) patients taking each day? 44% of all OxyContin  prescriptions are for 20 mg and 40 mg tablets strengths.1 For many patients taking OxyContin  20 mg or 40 mg tablets, converting to EXALGO may reduce the pill burden. See the conversion charts below:

 

Please see IMPORTANT RISK INFORMATION, including boxed warning.

Please see Full Prescribing Information for EXALGO.

 

For Your Opioid-Tolerant Chronic Pain Patients

EXALGO Offers Once-Daily Dosing With Potentially Fewer Pills



 



 

Generally, reduce the calculated equianalgesic dose by 25% to 50% to obtain the starting

dose2-4*

 

*In the pivotal trial, a 25% dose reduction of equianalgesic dose was used to determine a starting dose.2,3

 

Please see IMPORTANT RISK INFORMATION, including boxed warning.

Please see Full Prescribing Information for EXALGO.

 

Effectively Transition Patients to EXALGO  (hydromorphone HCl) Extended-Release Tablets (CII)

1. SET expectations

          There is no immediate-release component; plasma levels rise for the first 6 to 8 hours after the initial dose.2

          It takes 3 to 4 days to reach steady state.2,5

          Prescribe supplemental pain medication to help your patients get to steady state, through titration, and as needed thereafter.

 

2. START with an appropriate dose

Consider the reasons for switching when calculating a starting dose.
Generally, reduce the calculated equianalgesic dose by 25% to 50% to obtain the starting dose.2-4 
EXALGO is available in 8, 12, 16, and 32 mg tablets to provide flexibility when determining a starting dose; all tablets should be taken together once daily.2

 

3. TITRATE to an effective dose

Titration should not occur more frequently than every 3 to 4 days.2
If more than 2 doses of supplemental medication are needed for 2 consecutive days, it may be time to titrate upward.2
When titrating, consider a 25% to 50% increase in dose.2
It may take multiple titration steps to achieve effective pain control with tolerable side effects.

 

 In the pivotal trial, a 25% dose reduction of equianalgesic dose was used to determine a starting dose.2,3

 

Please see IMPORTANT RISK INFORMATION, including boxed warning.

EXALGO  (hydromorphone HCl) Extended-Release Tablets (CII) is indicated for the management of moderate to severe pain in opioid tolerant patients requiring continuous, around-the-clock opioid analgesia for an extended period of time.

EXALGO contains hydromorphone, an opioid agonist and a Schedule II controlled substance with an abuse liability similar to other opioid agonists, legal or illicit. Assess each patient s risk for opioid abuse or addiction prior to prescribing EXALGO. The risk for opioid abuse is increased in patients with a personal or family history of substance abuse (including drug or alcohol abuse or addiction) or mental illness (e.g., major depressive disorder). Routinely monitor all patients receiving EXALGO for signs of misuse, abuse, and addiction during treatment.

Respiratory depression, including fatal cases, may occur with use of EXALGO, even when the drug has been used as recommended and not misused or abused. EXALGO is for use in opioid tolerant patients only. Proper dosing and titration are essential and EXALGO should be prescribed only by healthcare professionals who are knowledgeable in the use of potent opioids for the management of chronic pain. Monitor for respiratory depression, especially during initiation of EXALGO or following a dose increase. Crushing, dissolving, or chewing the tablet can cause rapid release and absorption of a potentially fatal dose of hydromorphone.

Accidental ingestion of EXALGO, especially in children, can result in a fatal overdose of hydromorphone.


 

          EXALGO is contraindicated in:

-         Opioid non-tolerant patients. Fatal respiratory depression could occur in patients who are not opioid tolerant.

-         Patients with significant respiratory depression

-         Patients with acute or severe bronchial asthma in an unmonitored setting or in the absence of resuscitative equipment

-         Patients with known or suspected paralytic ileus

-         Patients who have had surgical procedures and/or underlying disease resulting in narrowing of the gastrointestinal tract, or have  blind loops  of the gastrointestinal tract or gastrointestinal obstruction

-         Patients with hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to hydromorphone or sulfite-containing medications

 

          EXALGO is indicated for opioid tolerant patients only. Patients considered opioid tolerant are those who are taking at least 60 mg oral morphine per day, 25 mcg transdermal fentanyl/hour, 30 mg oral oxycodone/day, 8 mg oral hydromorphone/day, 25 mg oral oxymorphone/day or an equianalgesic dose of another opioid, for a week or longer.

 

          EXALGO  (hydromorphone HCl) Extended-Release Tablets (CII) is not intended for use as an as-needed analgesic and is not indicated for the management of acute or postoperative pain. It is contraindicated in patients who need management of mild pain or pain not expected to persist.

Concurrent use of EXALGO with CNS depressants, including alcohol, increases risk of respiratory depression, hypotension, and profound sedation, potentially resulting in coma or death. EXALGO may impair the ability to drive a car or operate machinery.

From: Patrick, Jeffrey
